source_caption:
🎬 Jerry Maguire (1996)

Jerry Maguire follows a successful sports agent whose life takes an unexpected turn after he experiences a crisis of conscience about the ruthless business practices of his industry. When Jerry writes a heartfelt mission statement calling for fewer clients and more personal attention, he loses his prestigious job and nearly everything he has worked for. Determined to rebuild his career, he starts his own agency with the support of Dorothy Boyd, a single mother who believes in his vision, and Rod Tidwell, an outspoken football player determined to secure the contract he deserves. As Jerry struggles to balance professional ambition, romantic relationships, and personal integrity, he begins discovering what truly matters in life. Combining heartfelt romance, memorable comedy, emotional drama, and inspiring sports moments, the film explores loyalty, love, friendship, ambition, and the importance of staying true to yourself.

🎭 Genre: Romance • Comedy • Drama • Sports

⭐ IMDb: 7.3/10

⏱️ Runtime: 2h 19m • R

🎥 Director: Cameron Crowe

🏆 Recognition: Starring Tom Cruise, Renée Zellweger, and Cuba Gooding Jr., the film received five Academy Award nominations and won Best Supporting Actor for Cuba Gooding Jr. It became a beloved 1990s classic, famous for unforgettable lines including “Show me the money!” and “You had me at hello.”

📺 Where to Watch: Check Amazon Prime Video, Apple TV, and Fandango at Home for current streaming, rental, or purchase availability. Availability varies by region.

source_details.synopsis: Jerry Maguire is a 1996 American sports romantic comedy-drama film directed and written by Cameron Crowe. It was produced by Crowe and James L. Brooks, respectively for Vinyl Films and Gracie Films and distributed by Sony Pictures Releasing under the TriStar Pictures label. It stars Tom Cruise as the title character, alongside Cuba Gooding Jr., Renée Zellweger, Kelly Preston, Jerry O'Connell, Jay Mohr, Bonnie Hunt and Regina King. It was released in North American theaters on December 13, 1996.
